name: Forward Price (Cost-of-Carry, Continuous)
description: Computes the no-arbitrage forward price under continuous compounding as the spot price grown at the net cost of carry, S*exp((r - q)*T). The risk-free rate raises it while the dividend or convenience yield lowers it.
notes: r and q are continuously compounded annual rates as decimals and T is in years. If q exceeds r the forward trades below spot (backwardation).

name: Futures Price (Discrete Carry)
description: Computes a futures price under discrete compounding by adding the present value of carrying costs to the spot price and compounding at the risk-free rate, (S + U)*(1 + r)^T. Storage and financing costs push the futures above spot.
notes: U is the present value of carrying costs in the same currency as S, and r is a per-period rate as a decimal with T in matching periods. Income yields would be subtracted instead.

name: Black-Scholes d1
description: Computes the d1 term of the Black-Scholes option model, (ln(S/K) + (r + sigma^2/2)*T)/(sigma*sqrt(T)). It is the standardized distance of the log spot-to-strike ratio, and N(d1) gives the option's delta for a call.
notes: r and sigma are annualized decimals and T is in years, all measured over the same horizon. This assumes no dividends; a dividend yield would subtract from the drift term.

name: Black-Scholes d2
description: Computes the d2 term of the Black-Scholes model as d1 minus sigma times the square root of time, d1 - sigma*sqrt(T). N(d2) is the risk-neutral probability that a call finishes in the money.
notes: Feed in the d1 already computed for the same option, with sigma as an annualized decimal and T in years. d2 is always less than d1 by the volatility term sigma*sqrt(T).

name: Put-Call Parity (Implied Call Value)
description: Uses put-call parity to derive the European call value from the put price, spot, and the present value of the strike, P + S - K*exp(-r*T). It enforces the no-arbitrage relationship linking calls, puts, and the underlying.
notes: Applies to European options on a non-dividend-paying asset with matching strike and expiry. r is a continuously compounded decimal rate and T is in years.

name: Black-Scholes Gamma
description: Computes the Black-Scholes gamma, the rate of change of option delta with respect to the spot price, exp(-d1^2/2)/(S*sigma*sqrt(2*pi*T)). Gamma peaks for at-the-money options and fades as expiry nears for others.
notes: Uses the standard normal density of d1. Gamma is identical for a call and its matching put; sigma is annualized and T is in years. Assumes no dividends.

name: Black-Scholes Vega
description: Computes the Black-Scholes vega, the sensitivity of option value to a change in volatility, S*exp(-d1^2/2)*sqrt(T)/sqrt(2*pi). It shows how much the option premium rises when implied volatility increases.
notes: Uses the standard normal density of d1. Vega is the same for a call and its matching put and is largest for at-the-money, longer-dated options. T is in years; assumes no dividends.

name: Black–Scholes–Merton Call Price
expression: S * exp(-q * T) * normcdf(((ln(S / K) + (r - q + sigma^2 / 2) * T) / (sigma * sqrt(T)))) - K * exp(-r * T) * normcdf(((ln(S / K) + (r - q - sigma^2 / 2) * T) / (sigma * sqrt(T))))
description: Prices a European call on a stock paying a continuous dividend yield q (Black–Scholes 1973, Merton 1973).
notes: With S = K = 100, r = 5 %, σ = 20 %, one year and no dividends the call is worth about 10.4506.

name: Black–Scholes–Merton Put Price
expression: K * exp(-r * T) * normcdf(-((ln(S / K) + (r - q - sigma^2 / 2) * T) / (sigma * sqrt(T)))) - S * exp(-q * T) * normcdf(-((ln(S / K) + (r - q + sigma^2 / 2) * T) / (sigma * sqrt(T))))
description: Prices a European put with the Black–Scholes–Merton formula.
notes: For the standard example (S = K = 100, 5 %, 20 %, one year) the put is worth about 5.5735, consistent with put–call parity.

name: Call Delta (Black–Scholes)
expression: exp(-q * T) * normcdf(((ln(S / K) + (r - q + sigma^2 / 2) * T) / (sigma * sqrt(T))))
description: Gives the change in the call price per unit change in the underlying price: e^(−qT) N(d₁).
notes: Also the number of shares to hold to hedge one short call.

name: Put Delta (Black–Scholes)
expression: exp(-q * T) * (normcdf(((ln(S / K) + (r - q + sigma^2 / 2) * T) / (sigma * sqrt(T)))) - 1)
description: Gives the sensitivity of the put price to the underlying price: e^(−qT)(N(d₁) − 1), always negative.
notes: Call delta minus put delta equals e^(−qT).

name: Call Theta per Year (Black–Scholes)
expression: -S * exp(-q * T) * normpdf(((ln(S / K) + (r - q + sigma^2 / 2) * T) / (sigma * sqrt(T)))) * sigma / (2 * sqrt(T)) - r * K * exp(-r * T) * normcdf(((ln(S / K) + (r - q - sigma^2 / 2) * T) / (sigma * sqrt(T)))) + q * S * exp(-q * T) * normcdf(((ln(S / K) + (r - q + sigma^2 / 2) * T) / (sigma * sqrt(T))))
description: Gives the rate at which the call loses value as time passes, per year. Divide by 365 for the daily decay.
notes: About −6.41 a year (−0.0176 a day) in the standard example.

name: Put Theta per Year (Black–Scholes)
expression: -S * exp(-q * T) * normpdf(((ln(S / K) + (r - q + sigma^2 / 2) * T) / (sigma * sqrt(T)))) * sigma / (2 * sqrt(T)) + r * K * exp(-r * T) * normcdf(-((ln(S / K) + (r - q - sigma^2 / 2) * T) / (sigma * sqrt(T)))) - q * S * exp(-q * T) * normcdf(-((ln(S / K) + (r - q + sigma^2 / 2) * T) / (sigma * sqrt(T))))
description: Gives the time decay of a European put per year.
notes: Deep in-the-money European puts can have positive theta.

name: Call Rho (Black–Scholes)
expression: K * T * exp(-r * T) * normcdf(((ln(S / K) + (r - q - sigma^2 / 2) * T) / (sigma * sqrt(T))))
description: Gives the change in the call price per unit change in the interest rate (divide by 100 for one percentage point).
notes: About 53.2 in the standard example, i.e. +0.53 per 1 % rise in rates.

name: Put Rho (Black–Scholes)
expression: -K * T * exp(-r * T) * normcdf(-((ln(S / K) + (r - q - sigma^2 / 2) * T) / (sigma * sqrt(T))))
description: Gives the sensitivity of the put price to the interest rate; puts lose value when rates rise.
notes: About −41.9 in the standard example.

name: Probability a Call Finishes In the Money
expression: normcdf(((ln(S / K) + (r - q - sigma^2 / 2) * T) / (sigma * sqrt(T))))
description: Gives the risk-neutral probability N(d₂) that the underlying ends above the strike.
notes: Not the real-world probability, which uses the expected return instead of r.

name: Cash-or-Nothing Digital Call
expression: cash * exp(-r * T) * normcdf(((ln(S / K) + (r - q - sigma^2 / 2) * T) / (sigma * sqrt(T))))
description: Prices a binary option paying a fixed cash amount if the underlying ends above the strike.
notes: Digital options are the building blocks of many structured products.

name: Asset-or-Nothing Call
expression: S * exp(-q * T) * normcdf(((ln(S / K) + (r - q + sigma^2 / 2) * T) / (sigma * sqrt(T))))
description: Prices an option that pays the asset itself if it ends above the strike. A vanilla call is this minus K cash-or-nothing calls.
notes: About 63.7 in the standard example.

name: Implied Volatility of a Call
expression: solve(v, 0.001, 3, S * exp(-q * T) * normcdf((ln(S / K) + (r - q + v^2 / 2) * T) / (v * sqrt(T))) - K * exp(-r * T) * normcdf((ln(S / K) + (r - q - v^2 / 2) * T) / (v * sqrt(T))) - c)
description: Finds the volatility that makes the Black–Scholes call price equal the market price.
notes: Implied volatility is how options are actually quoted; plotting it against strike gives the volatility smile.

name: Black-76 Call on a Futures Price
expression: exp(-r * T) * (fut * normcdf((ln(fut / K) + sigma^2 * T / 2) / (sigma * sqrt(T))) - K * normcdf((ln(fut / K) - sigma^2 * T / 2) / (sigma * sqrt(T))))
description: Prices a European call on a futures or forward price (Black 1976), the market standard for commodity options, caps and swaptions.
notes: Equivalent to Black–Scholes with the dividend yield equal to r.

name: Black-76 Put on a Futures Price
expression: exp(-r * T) * (K * normcdf(-(ln(fut / K) - sigma^2 * T / 2) / (sigma * sqrt(T))) - fut * normcdf(-(ln(fut / K) + sigma^2 * T / 2) / (sigma * sqrt(T))))
description: Prices a European put on a futures price with Black's 1976 model.
notes: Floors on interest rates are priced as portfolios of such puts.

name: Garman–Kohlhagen FX Call
expression: S * exp(-rf * T) * normcdf((ln(S / K) + (rd - rf + sigma^2 / 2) * T) / (sigma * sqrt(T))) - K * exp(-rd * T) * normcdf((ln(S / K) + (rd - rf - sigma^2 / 2) * T) / (sigma * sqrt(T)))
description: Prices a European currency call; the foreign interest rate plays the role of a dividend yield.
notes: Quoted in domestic currency per unit of foreign currency.

name: Bachelier (Normal Model) Call
expression: exp(-r * T) * ((fut - K) * normcdf((fut - K) / (sn * sqrt(T))) + sn * sqrt(T) * normpdf((fut - K) / (sn * sqrt(T))))
description: Prices a call when the forward moves by normally distributed amounts (Bachelier 1900). Used for interest-rate options since rates went negative.
notes: Normal volatility is quoted in absolute terms (basis points per year), not as a percentage.

name: Put–Call Parity: Put from Call
expression: c - S * exp(-q * T) + K * exp(-r * T)
description: Gives the European put price implied by a call with the same strike and expiry: P = C − S e^(−qT) + K e^(−rT).
notes: Holds without any model; a gap signals an arbitrage (or dividends, borrowing costs, early exercise).

name: Binomial Tree Up Factor (Cox–Ross–Rubinstein)
description: Gives the up-move factor u = e^(σ√Δt) of a Cox–Ross–Rubinstein binomial tree; the down factor is 1/u.
notes: The tree converges to Black–Scholes as the number of steps grows.

name: Binomial Risk-Neutral Probability
expression: (exp((r - q) * T / n) - exp(-sigma * sqrt(T / n))) / (exp(sigma * sqrt(T / n)) - exp(-sigma * sqrt(T / n)))
description: Gives the risk-neutral probability of an up move in a CRR tree: (e^((r−q)Δt) − d)/(u − d).
notes: Must lie between 0 and 1; if not, use more steps.

name: European Call by an n-Step Binomial Tree
expression: exp(-r * T) * sum(k, 0, n, binom(n, k) * ((exp(r * T / n) - exp(-sigma * sqrt(T / n))) / (exp(sigma * sqrt(T / n)) - exp(-sigma * sqrt(T / n))))^k * (1 - (exp(r * T / n) - exp(-sigma * sqrt(T / n))) / (exp(sigma * sqrt(T / n)) - exp(-sigma * sqrt(T / n))))^(n - k) * max(S * exp(sigma * sqrt(T / n) * (2 * k - n)) - K, 0))
description: Prices a European call on a Cox–Ross–Rubinstein tree by weighting each final payoff with its binomial probability and discounting.
notes: With 200 steps the result is within about 0.01 of Black–Scholes (10.4506). Keep n below about 1000.

name: Margrabe Exchange Option
description: Prices the right to swap asset 2 for asset 1 at expiry (Margrabe 1978); interest rates drop out.
notes: The effective volatility is √(σ₁² + σ₂² − 2ρσ₁σ₂).

name: Perpetual American Put
expression: if(S <= K * 2 * r / sigma^2 / (1 + 2 * r / sigma^2), K - S, (K - K * 2 * r / sigma^2 / (1 + 2 * r / sigma^2)) * (S / (K * 2 * r / sigma^2 / (1 + 2 * r / sigma^2)))^(-2 * r / sigma^2))
description: Prices an American put that never expires (Merton 1973): exercise when the price falls to S* = Kβ/(1 + β), with β = 2r/σ².
notes: One of the few American options with a closed-form value.

name: Geometric Average Asian Call (Continuous)
expression: exp(-r * T) * (S * exp((r - q - sigma^2 / 6) * T / 2) * normcdf((ln(S / K) + ((r - q - sigma^2 / 6) / 2 + sigma^2 / 6) * T) / (sigma / sqrt(3) * sqrt(T))) - K * normcdf((ln(S / K) + ((r - q - sigma^2 / 6) / 2 - sigma^2 / 6) * T) / (sigma / sqrt(3) * sqrt(T))))
description: Prices a call on the continuous geometric average of the price (Kemna–Vorst 1990); the average has volatility σ/√3.
notes: A lower bound and control variate for the arithmetic Asian option, which has no closed form.

name: Option Intrinsic Value (Call)
description: Gives what a call would pay if exercised now.
notes: The rest of the option price is time value.

name: Option Time Value
description: Splits an option price into intrinsic value and the remaining time value.
notes: Time value is largest at the money and shrinks to zero at expiry.

name: Expected One-Standard-Deviation Move
description: Estimates the size of a one-standard-deviation price move over the coming days from the implied volatility.
notes: About 68 % of moves stay within this range under a normal approximation. Traders often use 252 trading days instead of 365.

name: Straddle Break-even Points (Upper)
description: Gives the upper price at which a long straddle (call and put at the same strike) breaks even at expiry; the lower one is K minus the total premium.
notes: The position profits if the price moves more than the total premium either way.

name: Forward Contract Value
description: Values an existing long forward contract: the difference between today's forward price and the agreed price, discounted.
notes: A new forward is worth zero because its delivery price equals the forward price.

name: Covered Interest Parity Forward FX Rate
description: Gives the no-arbitrage forward exchange rate from the spot rate and the two money-market rates (simple interest).
notes: The currency with the higher interest rate trades at a forward discount.

name: Forward Points
description: Gives the forward premium or discount in pips (units of 0.0001) that dealers quote instead of the outright forward rate.
notes: For yen pairs one pip is 0.01, so multiply by 100 instead of 10,000.

name: Cross Exchange Rate
description: Derives the A→C exchange rate by going through a common currency B.
notes: EUR/USD 1.08 and USD/JPY 160.5 give EUR/JPY 173.34. A mismatch with the direct quote would allow triangular arbitrage.

name: Minimum-Variance Hedge Ratio
description: Gives the number of futures units per unit of exposure that minimises the variance of the hedged position: h* = ρσ_S/σ_F.
notes: It is the slope of a regression of spot changes on futures changes.

name: Number of Futures Contracts to Hedge
description: Gives the optimal number of futures contracts: hedge ratio times exposure size divided by contract size.
notes: Round to a whole number of contracts in practice.

name: Beta Hedge with Index Futures
description: Gives the number of index futures to buy (positive) or sell (negative) to move a portfolio's beta to a target.
notes: Selling 24 contracts here makes the 5,000,000 portfolio market-neutral.

name: Futures Basis
description: Gives the basis, spot minus futures price. It converges to zero at delivery.
notes: Unexpected changes in the basis are the risk that remains in a futures hedge.

name: Options Payoff of a Bull Call Spread
description: Gives the profit at expiry of buying a call at K₁ and selling one at K₂ > K₁.
notes: Maximum profit K₂ − K₁ − premium; maximum loss the premium paid.

name: Iron Condor Maximum Loss-to-Profit Ratio
description: Gives the ratio of the maximum loss (width minus credit) to the maximum profit (the credit) of an iron condor or credit spread.
notes: A 5-wide spread sold for 1.5 risks 3.5 to make 1.5 (ratio about 2.33).

name: Cash-or-Nothing Digital Put
expression: cash * exp(-r * T) * normcdf(-((ln(S / K) + (r - sigma^2 / 2) * T) / (sigma * sqrt(T))))
description: Prices a binary option paying a fixed amount if the underlying ends below the strike.
notes: A digital call plus a digital put with the same strike is worth the discounted payout.

name: Implied Volatility of a Put
expression: solve(v, 0.001, 3, K * exp(-r * T) * normcdf(-(ln(S / K) + (r - v^2 / 2) * T) / (v * sqrt(T))) - S * normcdf(-(ln(S / K) + (r + v^2 / 2) * T) / (v * sqrt(T))) - p)
description: Finds the volatility at which the Black–Scholes put price equals the market price (no dividends).
notes: By put–call parity a put and a call with the same strike have the same implied volatility.

name: Option Elasticity (Call Omega)
expression: normcdf(((ln(S / K) + (r + sigma^2 / 2) * T) / (sigma * sqrt(T)))) * S / (S * normcdf(((ln(S / K) + (r + sigma^2 / 2) * T) / (sigma * sqrt(T)))) - K * exp(-r * T) * normcdf(((ln(S / K) + (r - sigma^2 / 2) * T) / (sigma * sqrt(T)))))
description: Gives the percentage change in the call price per 1 % change in the underlying: Δ·S/C.
notes: Explains why options are leveraged: about 6.1 in the standard example.

name: Chooser Option (Simple, No Dividends)
expression: S * normcdf(((ln(S / K) + (r + sigma^2 / 2) * T) / (sigma * sqrt(T)))) - K * exp(-r * T) * normcdf(((ln(S / K) + (r - sigma^2 / 2) * T) / (sigma * sqrt(T)))) + K * exp(-r * T) * normcdf(-(ln(S / K) + r * T - sigma^2 * tc / 2) / (sigma * sqrt(tc))) - S * normcdf(-(ln(S / K) + r * T + sigma^2 * tc / 2) / (sigma * sqrt(tc)))
description: Prices an option whose holder decides at time t whether it becomes a call or a put (Rubinstein 1991): a call to T plus a put to t with strike K e^(−r(T−t)).
notes: Worth more than either a call or a put alone, less than a straddle.

name: Forward-Start Call
expression: S * (normcdf((-ln(alpha) + (r + sigma^2 / 2) * (T - t1)) / (sigma * sqrt(T - t1))) - alpha * exp(-r * (T - t1)) * normcdf((-ln(alpha) + (r - sigma^2 / 2) * (T - t1)) / (sigma * sqrt(T - t1))))

variables.label: Strike as a fraction of the future spot α

description: Prices a call that starts at t₁ with its strike set to α times the spot at that date (no dividends); used in employee stock options and cliquets.
notes: Its value is S times the price of a call with S = 1 and K = α over the remaining life.

name: Black Caplet Price
expression: nom * tau_y * exp(-r * T) * (fwd * normcdf((ln(fwd / K) + sigma^2 * T / 2) / (sigma * sqrt(T))) - K * normcdf((ln(fwd / K) - sigma^2 * T / 2) / (sigma * sqrt(T))))
description: Prices one caplet, a call on a forward interest rate paid at the end of its accrual period, with Black's model.
notes: A cap is a series of caplets; a floorlet uses the corresponding put.

name: Put–Call Parity for Futures Options
description: Gives the call price minus the put price for European options on a futures contract with the same strike and expiry.
notes: A deviation signals mispricing between the options and the futures.

name: Covered Call If-Called Return
description: Gives the return of buying a stock and selling a call if the stock ends above the strike and is called away.
notes: Upside is capped at the strike; the premium cushions small falls.

name: Protective Put Maximum Loss
description: Gives the most a stock-plus-put position can lose per share: the drop to the strike plus the premium.
notes: The put works like an insurance policy with a deductible of S₀ − K.

name: Long Call Break-even Price
description: Gives the price the underlying must exceed at expiry for a bought call to make money.
notes: For a bought put the break-even is K − premium.

name: Parkinson Volatility (High–Low)
description: Estimates annualised volatility from daily high and low prices (Parkinson 1980), about five times more efficient than close-to-close.
notes: Assumes no drift and continuous trading.

name: Garman–Klass Volatility (OHLC)
expression: sqrt(mean(0.5 * ln(hi / lo)^2 - (2 * ln(2) - 1) * ln(cl / op)^2)) * sqrt(ppy)
description: Estimates annualised volatility from open, high, low and close prices (Garman–Klass 1980).
notes: More efficient than using closing prices alone.

name: Variance Swap Payoff
description: Gives the payoff of a variance swap: notional times realised variance (annualised, zero-mean convention) minus the variance strike.
notes: Vega notional equals variance notional × 2K.

name: Carry Trade Excess Return
description: Gives the return of borrowing in a low-rate currency to invest in a high-rate one, including the currency move.
notes: Uncovered interest parity says the currency should fall enough to remove the gain; in practice it often does not.

name: Non-Deliverable Forward Settlement
description: Gives the USD cash settlement of a non-deliverable forward on a restricted currency.
notes: Positive means the party that bought USD forward receives it.

name: Annualised FX Hedging Cost
description: Annualises the forward premium or discount, which is the cost or gain of hedging a currency exposure.
notes: It roughly equals the interest-rate differential between the two currencies.

name: Convenience Yield from Futures Prices
description: Backs out the convenience yield, the benefit of holding the physical commodity, from spot and futures prices.
notes: A high convenience yield (backwardation) signals tight supplies.

name: Spark Spread
description: Gives the gross margin of a gas-fired power plant: electricity price minus the cost of the gas burned.
notes: Clean spark spreads also subtract carbon costs.

name: 3-2-1 Crack Spread
description: Gives the refining margin per barrel when three barrels of crude yield two of gasoline and one of distillate.
notes: Product prices are converted from gallons at 42 gallons per barrel.

name: Long Butterfly Payoff
expression: max(S - k1, 0) - 2 * max(S - k2, 0) + max(S - k3, 0) - net
description: Gives the expiry profit of buying calls at K₁ and K₃ and selling two at K₂ (equally spaced).
notes: Profits most when the price ends at the middle strike.

name: Bear Put Spread Payoff
description: Gives the expiry profit of buying a put at K₂ and selling one at K₁ < K₂.
notes: Maximum profit K₂ − K₁ − premium if the price falls below K₁.

name: Collar Profit (Stock + Long Put + Short Call)
expression: S - s0 + max(kp - S, 0) - max(S - kc, 0) - net
description: Gives the expiry profit per share of holding a stock with a protective put financed by a covered call.
notes: Locks the outcome between kp − s0 and kc − s0 (here −10 to +10).

name: Futures Margin Call Price (Long)
description: Gives the futures price at which a long position receives a margin call (the account falls to the maintenance margin).
notes: For a short position the call comes at f₀ + (IM − MM)/size.
